Q: Trait or abstract class with a self-referential generic type for an implicit A:

Yes, this is possible. The key is an abstract class that has a type parameter, an implicit constructor parameter, and a self-type. The self-type forces each subclass to pass itself as the type parameter. I compiled and ran the code below with Scala 2.13.18 and fixed-length 1.1.0, and the output is the same as your original.

sealed trait Record {
  def encode: String
}

sealed abstract class EncodedRecord[R](implicit enc: Encoder[R]) extends Record { this: R =>
  final override def encode: String = enc.encode(this)
}

case class A(a: String, b: Int) extends EncodedRecord[A]

case class B(a: String, b: Int) extends EncodedRecord[B]

The implicit encoder definitions stay unchanged. records can keep the type Seq[Record].

How this works:

  • A trait cannot have constructor parameters in Scala 2. Thus the shared code lives in an abstract class.
  • The compiler resolves the implicit Encoder[R] once, at the definition site of each subclass. Each instance then captures its own encoder.
  • The self-type this: R => gives this the type R inside the class body. Thus enc.encode(this) type-checks. It also prevents a mistake such as class B extends EncodedRecord[A] — that does not compile.
  • The extra EncodedRecord layer keeps the Record trait free of type parameters. If you do not need the plain trait, you can put the type parameter on Record directly. The sequence then becomes a Seq[Record[_]].

An alternative, if you prefer no type parameters at all: keep your original trait and write one Encoder[Record] that pattern-matches on the sealed subclasses. The compiler then warns you when a new subclass is missing from the match. But the class-based solution above removes all per-subclass repetition, so I would recommend it.

Q: Placing characters at a specific column in vi A:

You can add two horizontal lines and some spaces as following:

:%s/^/  
:%s/\_.*/-\r&-
:%g/-/norm gn20A-
:%g/.*/normal 20A

Then sorround it by ! characters at desired column number (for example \%>17c):

:%s/^\|\%>17c.*/!/g

Q: What is a ".NET identity"? A:

Two instances of a class are "identical" if they are actually the same instance (same memory location).
The default implementation IMHO calls Object.ReferenceEquals.

Two structures are "identical" if their values are all equal meaning they are bitwise identical.
The default implementation here uses refletion to compare all members IMHO.

However, both behaviors can be overriden using the Equals method.
